body:
You seem to have caught a few of these already, but the ones using `new`/`delete` in the `jolt_physics` module are doing so deliberately, as a lot of classes from Jolt itself override `new`/`delete` on a per-class basis, which will end up calling either the `JPH::Alloc` callback or `JPH::AlignedAlloc` callback (which call `Memory::alloc_static` and `Memory::alloc_aligned_static` respectively) based on their alignment requirements, which `memnew`/`memdelete` would not respect.

Therefore, as a general rule, I opted to not use `memnew`/`memdelete` for any type that either comes directly from Jolt, or which is inheriting from a Jolt type, even if they did not in fact override `new`/`delete`, on the off-chance that they one day might.

However, this does mean that something like the `jolt_settings` member found in `JoltArea3D`, `JoltBody3D` and `JoltSoftBody3D` do not in fact go through `memnew`/`memdelete`, as those types don't currently override their `new`/`delete`, which is likely not great, as they will be plentiful in numbers yet won't be tracked, so I'd be fine with leaving those particular changes in. The rest are either not correct or too few in practical allocation size/amount to matter at all.

EDIT: As a sidenote, I've been meaning to look into adding tracking to `Memory::alloc_aligned_static`, since some Jolt-related allocations do go through that function, and which currently bypasses the memory tracking.
